questions.question: What is the main purpose of a trend-following strategy?
options: To predict every market top and bottom
To trade in the direction of an established market trend
To trade only during sideways markets
To avoid using stop-losses
questions.explanation: Trend-following strategies aim to participate in an established direction rather than predicting every reversal.

questions.question: Which market structure normally represents an uptrend?
options: Lower Highs and Lower Lows
Equal Highs and Equal Lows
Higher Highs and Higher Lows
Higher Highs and Lower Lows
questions.explanation: An uptrend normally produces a sequence of Higher Highs and Higher Lows.

questions.question: Where should a range trader generally look for a buying opportunity?
options: Near confirmed support
Near confirmed resistance
In the middle of the range
Immediately after every large bullish candle
questions.explanation: Range traders generally look for confirmed buying opportunities near the lower support boundary.

questions.question: Which condition provides stronger evidence of a genuine bullish breakout?
options: A small wick above resistance followed by an immediate reversal
A strong candle close above resistance with momentum and follow-through
Price touching resistance without closing above it
A breakout occurring without any important market level
questions.explanation: A strong close above resistance, supported by momentum and follow-through, provides stronger breakout confirmation.

questions.question: What is an entry trigger?
options: The trader's emotional feeling about the market
The final predefined condition that activates a trade
The amount deposited into the trading account
The maximum leverage offered by the broker
questions.explanation: An entry trigger is the specific final condition that must occur before a trade is executed.

questions.question: What is the difference between an entry zone and an entry trigger?
options: There is no difference
The entry zone is where a setup may form, while the trigger confirms the actual entry
The entry zone determines leverage, while the trigger determines the broker
The trigger is always identified before the zone
questions.explanation: An entry zone identifies a possible location, while the entry trigger confirms when the trade should actually be opened.

questions.question: Which order type attempts to execute immediately at the best available current price?
options: Limit order
Market order
Stop-limit order
Pending cancellation order
questions.explanation: A market order attempts to execute immediately at the best available price.

questions.question: What should a trader do when price has already moved far beyond the planned entry and the original risk-to-reward is no longer available?
options: Increase the position size
Move the stop-loss farther away
Chase the trade immediately
Cancel the trade and wait for a new valid setup
questions.explanation: A trader should avoid chasing price and wait for a new setup when the original entry conditions are no longer valid.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a complete trading plan?
options: It only states which market to trade
It only explains where to place the take-profit
It defines the full process before, during and after trading
It guarantees that all trades will be profitable
questions.explanation: A complete trading plan covers market selection, setup rules, risk, execution, management, psychology, journaling and review.

questions.question: According to this course, which risk rule must remain part of every trading strategy?
options: Risk at least 10% during every session
Avoid calculating correlated exposure
Never exceed 5% total risk during one trading session
Always use the maximum leverage available
questions.explanation: The course establishes 5% of total trading capital as the maximum session-risk ceiling.
